comments.body: Might need 36575ba3b1f0d446a0ba4a6fdab61a0a472a67f5 from #7077 and its follow up, 7ae657d24988732d4afdef127cc83361db74c173 from #7081.
(@lsm5 this is still draft, and the testing-farm failures might not be flakes)

I saw a bunch of `Bad Gateway` in https://artifacts.dev.testing-farm.io/1aa4ee95-fc1c-4100-8f0e-e575cd147c7e/ . Let's see how much a rerun fixes. If we'd rather get this in sooner, let's ignore testing-farm given we have already passing GHA.

I think that the reason we're not seeing this error in CI is because in CI we stand up a local registry with cached copies of the images we use, and configure the local registry as the physical location for the images, while outside of CI we configure quay.io/libpod as a mirror for docker.io/library.

quay.io is having some trouble right now, so sometimes we pull an image from quay.io and cache it in an early test, then import it from the cache for use at the start of a later test, but the default pull policy combined with problems at the registry causes test commands to pull a newer version of the image from docker.io.  A test then sees two images, one of which used to have a name which now refers to a different image, and mistakes it for an intermediate image.

That would also explain why some tests which depend on busybox being statically-linked (which is more often the case in older versions of the image, like the ones we pushed to quay.io/libpod) are failing.
